text: Given a valid AlertOps API key header and open alerts exist, When alertops_list_alerts is called with no filters, Then it returns a paginated 'alerts' array (alert_id, status, priority, owner, created_date) capped at the default page size, with a has_more flag.
Given status=Open and priority=Critical filters, When alertops_list_alerts is called, Then only alerts matching both filters are returned.
Given an existing alert_id, When alertops_get_alert is called, Then the full alert detail (status, owner, escalation_policy, within_sla) is returned.
Given an alert_id that does not exist, When alertops_get_alert is called, Then a structured not_found error is returned, not a raw exception.
Given groups exist in the account, When alertops_list_groups is called with no filter, Then it returns group_id and group_name for each group, paginated.
Given a search term, When alertops_list_groups is called with that search value, Then only groups whose name matches are returned.
Given a group_id with members, When alertops_get_group_members is called, Then each member's name, member_type, and roles are returned.
Given a group_id with no members, When alertops_get_group_members is called, Then an empty members list is returned, not an error.
Given at least one group has an on-call member right now, When alertops_get_oncall_now is called with no group_id, Then it returns on-call members for every group.
Given a specific group_id, When alertops_get_oncall_now is called with that group_id, Then only that group's on-call members are returned.
Given a group_id and a start/end date within 3 months, When alertops_get_group_schedule is called, Then the schedule rotation entries covering that window are returned.
Given a date range exceeding AlertOps' 3-month schedule limit, When alertops_get_group_schedule is called, Then a structured invalid_argument error is returned before any call to AlertOps.
steps: Call alertops_get_group_schedule with an end_date more than 3 months after start_date against a real AlertOps account
Observe whether AlertOps' own API returns a 400 for the out-of-range window, or silently truncates/ignores the excess range
expect: Tool returns a structured invalid_argument error explaining the 3-month limit before calling AlertOps (client-side pre-check); confirming AlertOps' own upstream rejection shape needs a live account to compare against
evidence: Needs a real AlertOps vendor account; not available to this pipeline. Per vendor-mcp-development SOP, missing a test account does not block delivery to INT.

text: Given a request with no X-AlertOps-Api-Key header, When any tool is called, Then the server returns 401 with a body listing the required header, and makes no call to AlertOps.
Given AlertOps returns 401 for an invalid API key, When any tool is called, Then the tool returns the structured error envelope with code=unauthorized, not a raw exception.

Given AlertOps returns 429 or a 5xx, When any tool is called, Then the tool retries with backoff within the 120s budget and, if still failing, returns code=rate_limited or code=upstream_error respectively.

Given two concurrent requests carry different X-AlertOps-Api-Key header values, When both call alertops_list_alerts at the same time, Then each response only reflects its own header's AlertOps account, with no cross-request state leakage.
